proof.text: Use the existing fixed-scalar open restriction and extension adjunctions, transported through sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence. For the two complementary opens, cross restrictions of extension by zero are zero by ProEtale.isInitial_openImmersionRestriction_openImmersionLowerShriek. The two-open Zariski cover is a pro-etale cover; ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction makes its restrictions jointly conservative. Construct a quasi-inverse by the biproduct of the two extensions. The adjunction counits and units give the two isomorphisms, checked after restriction. The resulting equivalence preserves finite limits and colimits. This is pair_equivalence and clopenSectionComponentCore in the Lean proof.

Full faithfulness of extension by zero makes the open unit invertible. Cross restriction is zero, so extension maps to (M,0). Lift maps and differentials of a pair of complexes through the full faithful restriction pair. Faithfulness proves the complex equations; essential surjectivity chooses degreewise preimages and transports the differentials through the component isomorphisms. Exact restrictions commute with homology, so acyclicity is detected by the pair. Lift a pair of homotopies through the same Hom bijection; additivity and faithfulness prove their zero and homotopy equations. These are pair_complex_equivalence, pair_homotopy and clopenSectionComponentComplex.

The already proved ProEtale.isIso_openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar_of_isClosed_range identifies extension by zero with open direct image. Restriction is exact, hence its right adjoint preserves K-injectives. Transport this property through that isomorphism and the canonical coefficient equivalences. No degree bound is introduced.

Construct fixedSectionRestriction on each test object by restriction along clopenSectionComponentArrow. Pullback projection equations prove its naturality. Its composite with the open direct-image counit equals lowerStarComp followed by the section equality and lowerStarId; prove the equality by sheaf extensionality and the pullback universal properties. The clopen lowerShriek-to-lowerStar isomorphism makes this restriction invertible on extension-by-zero objects. Conjugate it through sfIntrinsicDirectImageComparison to obtain intrinsicSectionRestriction. Naturality of the realization unit and the uniquely normalized comparison prove the displayed scalar-unit section equation. Compose with the inverse open unit to construct the required natural isomorphism. This is clopenSectionComparison.

Apply mapHomologicalComplexCompIso and mapHomologicalComplexIdIso to this same natural isomorphism. Its degree components are definitionally the underived ones. Naturality proves the displayed chain-map and homotopy compatibilities. Assemble these results and the preceding component properties by conjunction introduction, with the original statement unchanged.

title: Clopen pro-etale component decomposition and K-injective insertion
statement:
Let $X,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:V\to X$ be a scheme morphism, and let $s:X\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with closed image and $qs=1_X$. Put $Z=V\setminus s(X)$ with open inclusion $t:Z\hookrightarrow V$. For a finite commutative ring $A$, use module sheaves over the constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restriction gives an exact equivalence
$$\operatorname{Mod}(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\times\operatorname{Mod}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A),\qquad F\mapsto(s^*F,t^*F),$$
under which extension by zero $s_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is the insertion $M\mapsto(M,0)$. The induced equivalence on unbounded cochain complexes carries acyclic complexes and chain homotopies componentwise. In particular, if $I$ is K-injective on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], then $s_!I$ is K-injective on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The ordinary direct image of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] has a natural isomorphism $q_*s_!M\cong M$ for every module sheaf $M$: on each site object $W\to X$ its map is restriction of sections on $V\times_XW$ to the component $s(X)\times_XW\cong W$. This isomorphism extends termwise to complexes and commutes with chain maps and homotopies.
